subject: Game Theory
title: Refugee Matching
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Refugee Matching.

hook.text: A Syrian family arrives in Europe. Which city should host them? Families have needs; cities have capacities.

buildup.text: Random assignment ignores preferences: a family needing Arabic schools lands in a town without them.

discovery.text: Economists designed matching algorithms: families rank cities, and cities specify quotas and priorities.

twist.text: Sweden and Switzerland piloted algorithm-based placement. Employment outcomes improved 40-70% versus random assignment.

climax.text: The mechanism respects both refugee preferences and community constraints. Design beats luck for life outcomes.

punchline.text: The right match changes a life's trajectory.

quiz.question: How do matching algorithms improve refugee placement?
options: They match family needs with city capacities
